info.name: Cable Backend — API v1
info.description:
Satya Cable & Broadband API.

Tokens are handled for you:
- Any response containing `accessToken` is captured into the environment.
- Before every authenticated request, the token is refreshed if it is missing or within 60s of expiry.
- A rejected refresh clears the environment, because replaying a rotated refresh token revokes the session (AGENTS.md §4.6).

Start with **Auth > OTP > Request code**, then **Verify code**.

exec: // Keeps {{accessToken}} fresh so no request is sent with a dead token.
// Refreshes when the token is missing, or within 60s of expiry.
// Sign-in endpoints mint tokens; refreshing before them would be circular.
console.warn('[auth] No refreshToken. Run "OTP > Verify" or "Login" first.');
// AUTH_REFRESH_REUSED means the session was revoked: the stored token is
// dead and reusing it would revoke the new session too.
console.log('[auth] token refreshed, valid for', data.expiresIn, 's');
// Captures tokens from any response that carries them, so Login, OTP Verify and
// Refresh all populate the environment without their own scripts.
try { body = pm.response.json(); } catch (e) { body = null; }
// `/auth/me` is the only response that names the caller's memberships.
// A member of more than one tenant MUST send x-tenant-id: without it every
'- set tenantId by hand to act in another one');
// On logout, clear session credentials from environment
try { body = pm.response.json(); } catch (e) { body = null; }

header.description: Send to populate the tenant-scoped customer profile when the user has memberships.

request.description:
The signed-in user, the session, and every tenant they are a member of with the role they hold there.

Also carries `customer`: the subscriber record in the **active** tenant — its primary address, every subscription joined through package → provider → service, and a `summary` a home screen can render on its own.

`customer` is `null` for staff (a login without a subscriber record), and for a caller who belongs to several tenants and sent no `x-tenant-id` — a customer record belongs to exactly one operator, so there is no single right answer.
Other accounts signed in on the same device stay signed in.
Revokes every session for this user across all devices.

item.description:
Sign-in answers with `memberships`: every tenant this user may act in, each with `tenantId`, `tenantName` and the `roleId` they hold there.

ONE membership: the API infers the tenant and `X-Tenant-Id` is noise.

SEVERAL: the client has to put the names in front of a human and send the chosen `X-Tenant-Id` on every request after that — without it a protected route answers 403, and `/auth/me` answers `customer: null` because there is no single right account to return.

item.name: Locations
item.description:
Tenant-configured address tree (AGENTS.md §8.6).

`X-Tenant-Id` is sent on every request here; it is only REQUIRED when your account belongs to more than one operator — otherwise the tenant comes from the token. Leave `tenantId` empty in the environment if you have a single membership.

Order for a fresh tenant: create categories → create a schema over them → create a root → generate the subtree.

request.description:
`parentId=null` lists roots. There is no separate /children route — that is what this parameter is.

Enable one of the disabled params for the other views:
- `parentId={{locationId}}` — one level down.
- `ancestorId={{locationId}}` — the whole subtree at any depth, the filter a customer dashboard uses.
- `q=Sai` — name OR alias, so `Sai Apartments`, `SSA` and `Sri Sai Apt` all find the same building.
- `categoryId` + `status=pending` — nodes a field operator added that nobody has approved yet.

A ROOT needs `schemaId` and an unrestricted grant — it sits inside nobody’s subtree:

```json
{ "schemaId": "{{schemaId}}", "name": "Mandapeta" }
```

A CHILD (the body below) inherits schema and category: the category is whatever the schema puts at the next level, so the client never picks one.

`aliases` replaces the whole set.

item.name: Customers
item.description:
The staff view. Both routes are `customers.view`, so the SCOPE on the grant decides what comes back — an admin’s ALL is the tenant, a field operator’s LOCATION is their areas, a subscriber’s OWN is themselves.

Every LIST item carries all searchable customer, account, location and equipment values. DETAIL adds the full billing graph.

query.description: Customer, account, address, location or equipment value.
That node AND everything under it.
Customers holding a line from this provider.
Keyset cursor from previous page (pass nextCursor until null).

request.description:
Every row carries all searchable customer, service-account, location and equipment values. Add `q` to rank the same response shape by fuzzy relevance.

Saves `customerId` from the first row.

Everything a details page draws, in one response: the customer, the breadcrumb, every subscription with its service, provider and package expanded, the equipment on loan, the last 20 ledger lines and a summary.

A customer id is a handle onto a graph. Walking it over the public endpoints would be six or more calls per page; this resolves it server-side where the joins are indexed.

Out of your area answers 404, not 403 — whether a customer exists elsewhere is not something the caller should learn.

item.name: Catalogue
item.description:

Order for a fresh tenant: create a service → add its providers → add packages to a provider → set coverage → check availability at a location.
